question: When 60 KJ heat is produced by a heater in 1 minute and 20 seconds then its power is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**750 W**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Given Values:
 
 
• Heat produced (Q) = **60 kJ **= **60000 J**
 
• Time Taken: The given time is** 1 minute **and **20 seconds**, which equals **80 seconds**.
 
 
 
• Formula for Power:
 
 
• Power is calculated as the total heat divided by time.
 
• **Power (P)** =** Q / t**
 
 
 
• Substitute the Values:
 
 
• **P = 60000 / 80**
 
 
 
• Calculating the Power:
 
 
• **P = 750 W**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Power **is the rate at which energy is transferred or converted and is measured in **watts **(**W**).
 
• **Heat **is a form of **energy**, and its rate of transfer determines the power of the system.
 
• The SI unit of power is the **watt (W)**, where **1 watt** equals **1 joule** **per second**.
 
• The heat generated in devices like **heaters **depends on **current**, **resistance**, and **voltage**.
 
• Power ratings of electrical appliances help determine their **energy consumption** and operational efficiency.
 
• Understanding power and heat transfer is crucial in designing efficient** heating systems** and **optimizing** energy usage.
